response.message:
I've drawn the incident-correlation flow on IBM Cloud: synthetic services send logs and traces to a collector, then a redaction step runs before the data is stored and indexed. The analysis runtime then sends only bounded, redacted evidence to watsonx.ai and returns a cited answer to the operator. The first local test would use synthetic logs that include planted secrets, a prompt-injection line, a missing span and a duplicate batch, with a scripted mock model. That only checks the plumbing. It can show that redaction, ID citations, tool blocking, uncertainty and timeline dedup work, but it says nothing about real watsonx.ai reasoning quality, which needs a separate labelled evaluation run. No region or account access has been checked or approved.

Should the AI only reason over evidence we've already fetched for it, with no tool calls at all? Or should it be allowed to request extra read-only searches through a fixed allowlist?

proposal.title: IBM Cloud log/trace incident analysis – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic log and trace collection, redaction before storage and model input, a versioned archive, search, an analysis runtime with a model call, and a cited answer for operators. Assumptions: region not selected yet; no account access, model entitlement or service interoperability has been verified. None of these IBM components has native Terraform coverage yet, so they are design-level and still need engineering work.

data.label: Synthetic services
data.description: Existing synthetic workloads that emit logs and OpenTelemetry traces. Log text is treated as untrusted.

data.label: OTel collector
data.description: OpenTelemetry Collector app on Code Engine. Receives logs and spans, adds batch IDs and a deterministic event key (trace_id/span_id/log_id plus hash) so repeated ingestion stays idempotent.

data.label: Redaction worker
data.description: Separate Code Engine job that masks secrets and tokens before anything is stored or sent to the model. Records redaction counts but never the original values.

data.label: Redacted event archive
data.description: Versioned bucket holding redacted batches keyed by event key, so the incident timeline can be rebuilt consistently.

data.label: Log/trace search index
data.description: Indexes redacted logs and spans by trace_id, span_id, log_id and timestamp. Upserts use the event key to prevent duplicates.

data.label: Incident analysis runtime
data.description: Builds the timeline, detects missing spans, and sends log text to the model as quoted data only, never as instructions. It has no write tools, and model output cannot trigger tool calls. A validator rejects any conclusion that does not cite an existing trace or log ID and returns 'uncertain' when there are gaps. It also serves the cited answer to operators.

data.label: LLM
data.description: Foundation model inference on redacted evidence only. The model choice, region availability and entitlement have not been checked yet.

data.label: Operator sign-in
data.description: Authenticates operators before they can use the analysis app.

data.label: On-call operator
data.description: Person asking about an incident and reviewing the cited answer.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If a secret leaks into a prompt or index, it is exposed beyond its original system.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Redact secrets before model input'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Secrets must be redacted before storage, indexing and any model input.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Lets operators check the evidence and catches invented causes.
requirementDrafts.basis: User criterion: 'Link conclusions to exact trace or log IDs'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Every conclusion must cite at least one existing trace or log ID. Answers without valid citations are rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stops a log line containing a prompt injection from taking actions.
requirementDrafts.basis: User criterion: 'Prompt injection in a log cannot issue tool calls'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Log content is treated as untrusted data. Model output cannot trigger tool calls or any write actions.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents confident but wrong incident explanations.
requirementDrafts.basis: User criterion: 'Missing spans yield uncertainty rather than invented causes'.
requirementDrafts.statement: When spans are missing, the answer reports uncertainty and the gap instead of a cause.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Retries and replays must not distort what happened during the incident.
requirementDrafts.basis: User criterion: 'Repeated ingestion preserves a consistent incident timeline'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Re-ingesting the same events produces the same incident timeline, with no duplicates.

response.message:
No runtime checks have run yet (0 checks, status "blocked"), so nothing has passed and the design isn't validated yet. The 8 blockers aren't design mistakes. The exporter has no native IBM implementation for the collector, redaction, archive, search, analysis runtime, watsonx.ai or App ID. Its only IBM contract is plain private object storage. Narrowing the design to that would drop the work you asked for, so I'm not proposing a graph change. Closing these gaps is product engineering work: typed IBM Code Engine, OpenSearch, watsonx.ai and App ID implementations, with this artifact (digest 97ac7030…) as the reproducer. The synthetic services also need a reference plan for an existing system.

Meanwhile, we can firm up the design. Should the analysis runtime only reason over evidence it has already fetched, with no tool calls? Or should it be allowed to run extra read-only searches from a fixed allowlist? Your answer changes how we enforce and test REQ-006, the prompt-injection requirement.
